title: Pauri 28, meaning: contentment for earrings
hookLine: make contentment your earrings, modesty your bowl, meditation your ashes; conquer the mind and you conquer the world (Japji 28)

cards: A nurse's scrubs, a judge's robe, a team jersey. Put one on and people know who you are. But everybody also knows the uniform isn't the job.
A jersey doesn't make the shot. Scrubs don't make you kind. Pauri 28 talks to the yogis about their uniform, and it's gentle, and it's direct.

teach.b: Pauri 28 goes through the yogi's outfit piece by piece, giving each one an inner meaning. In paraphrase: make contentment your earrings. Make effort and modesty your begging bag, and honor what you carry in it.

teach.h: MEDITATION FOR ASHES, FAITH A STAFF.
teach.b: Make meditation the ashes you smear on your body. Let the awareness of death be your patched coat. Keep your body pure, the way you'd keep a vow.
Let faith be your walking staff, and a right way of living your discipline. Then a line borrows the name of a yogi order and opens it wide. The Aaee Panth was one of the respected Nath sects.
Guru Nanak says, in paraphrase: let all people be your order, the whole of humanity your brotherhood.
And then the line behind today's carry, in the original: man jeetai jag jeet.
Conquer the mind, and you conquer the world. Every outer thing the yogi set out to master, the body, hunger, the world, comes down to one inner thing: the mind.
The stanza closes: aades tisai aades, salutation to Him, the primal one, pure, without beginning, beyond harm, the same through every age. How do Sikhs hear this?
Sikh tradition doesn't ask anyone to leave home for the forest. The Gurus lived as householders, with families and work.

Many Sikhs hear Pauri 28 as saying the discipline the yogi wore on the outside can be carried on the inside, anywhere, in a kitchen or an office. The earrings become contentment. The ashes become meditation.
And the whole world becomes your order.

how: Pauri 28 is recited in the morning Japji Sahib; many Sikhs quote man jeetai jag jeet, conquer the mind and you conquer the world, as a summary of living a disciplined inner life within family and work.

o: the stanza that turns the yogi's outfit inward
the stanza that tells the yogis to go home
a hymn listing the yogis' many mistakes

games.q: the outfit, turned inward — tap the pairs.

s: Pauri 28 says the mind is the key to everything the yogi sought
man jeetai jag jeet: conquer the mind and you conquer the world.
the Sikh Gurus lived as renunciants in the forest
they lived as householders, with families and work.
it takes each piece seriously and gives it an inner meaning.

games.q: you're a yogi who has worked for years to master the world. what does Pauri 28 say is the real conquest?
games.why: man jeetai jag jeet: conquer the mind, and you conquer the world.

practice: Choose one inner ornament to wear: contentment, modesty, honor, faith, or the steadiness of meditation, and picture putting it on the way you'd put on a ring or a coat. Breathe with it, and let it settle on you.
When the mind wanders, notice it and come back; that is the conquering, one return at a time.

wordCard.voice: Pauri 28. Contentment for earrings, meditation for ashes, faith for a staff, all people your order. Conquer the mind, and you conquer the world.

orig.note: Gurmukhi, Japji Pauri 28: conquer the mind, and you conquer the world.

carryVoice: Your line: conquer the mind. A whole week of Japji is behind you now. Day two hundred ten.

sources.ref: Guru Granth Sahib, Ang 6 (Japji, Pauri 28, the outfit lines and aades tisai aades)
